• **Equestrian sports:-**

 
 
• **These are sports that use horses as a main part of the sport. This usually takes the form of the rider being on the horse's back, or the horses pulling some sort of horse-drawn vehicle.**
 
• Equestrian sports are a popular form of recreation and competition around the world.
 
• There are many different types of equestrian sports, each with its own unique rules and challenges.
 
 
 
• **Dressage**:
 
 
• **Dressage is a sport in which the horse and rider perform a series of movements that demonstrate the horse's training and obedience. (Hence it is associated with Equestrian)**
 
• Dressage is often described as a dance between horse and rider.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **It is a team sport played on horseback, where the objective is to score goals against the opposing team by hitting a small ball into their goal with a long-handled mallet. **
 
• Each team has four players, and the game is typically played on a grass field.
 
 
 
• **Rugby:-**
 
 
• It is a team sport played with an oval ball.
 
• **The objective of the game is to score more points than the opposing team by grounding the ball over the opponent's try-line (scoring a try) or kicking the ball through the opponent's goalposts (scoring a conversion or penalty kick). **

questions.question: The committee to 'Operationalise the Suggestions to Teach Fundamental Duties to the Citizens of the Country' is popularly known as the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**J S Verma Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** J S Verma Committee:-**

 
 
• **The committee to 'Operationalise the Suggestions to Teach Fundamental Duties to the Citizens of the Country' was J S Verma Committee.**
 
• It was chaired by Justice J.S. Verma and was appointed by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in 1998.
 
• The committee made a number of recommendations on how to teach fundamental duties to citizens of all ages, including through school curricula, public awareness campaigns, and government programs.
 
• The J.S. Verma Committee's report also made a number of recommendations on other issues, such as reforming the police and the criminal justice system, and addressing the root causes of violence against women.
 
• These recommendations have not been fully implemented, but they continue to be relevant and important.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It was a committee appointed by the Government of India in 1978 **to examine the role and functioning of the Intelligence Bureau (IB), the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW).**
 
• The committee was headed by L.P. Singh, a former Director General of Police of Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Abhijit Sen Committee:-**
 
 
• It was a committee appointed by the Government of India in 2007 **to study the impact of futures trading on agricultural commodity prices.**
 
• The committee was headed by Abhijit Sen, a well-known economist and former member of the Planning Commission of India.
 
 
 
• **Paul Appleby Committee:-**

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Vernacular Press Act 1878:

 
 
• Lord Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act in 1878 to restrict vernacular newspapers from publishing any seditious material.
 
• The Act aimed to control the writings of Indians against the British policies and could excite dissatisfaction in the Indians against the British government.
 
• According to the Vernacular Press Act, any magistrate or police commissioner had the power to order any printer or publisher of a newspaper to sign a bond promising not to publish a specific type of material and to seize any printed materials it deemed offensive.
 
• The Act required that all proof sheets of a paper’s contents be submitted to the police before publication.
 
• Thus, the Act allowed the British government to keep track of the vernacular newspapers writing against the Britishers and opposing their policies.
 
• When a newspaper’s writing was considered “seditious”, the newspaper was first warned and had to face serious consequences the next time.

questions.question: GNP at MP less _____ gives us GDP at MP.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**net factor income from abroad**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Gross National Product at Market Price:-**

 
 
• It is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents in a given period, regardless of where they are located.
 
• GNP at MP less net factor income from abroad gives us GDP.
 
• Formula for it is **GNP at MP = GDP at MP + Net factor income from abroad**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP**:-

 
 
• It stands for Gross Domestic Product.
 
• **It is the total monetary value of all the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period. **
 
• It is one of the most important indicators of a country's economic health.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies**:-
 
 
• A subsidy is a financial benefit given by a government to a producer or consumer of a good or service.
 
• Subsidies can be direct or indirect. Direct subsidies are payments made to the producer or consumer, while indirect subsidies are tax breaks or other benefits that reduce the cost of production or consumption.
 
 
 
• **Indirect tax:-**
 
 
• **It is a tax that is levied on the consumption of goods and services. **
 
• It is not directly levied on the income of a person.

questions.question: Which of the following is the INCORRECT sequence of national income from broader to narrower concepts?

options.text: GNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost - NNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost
GNP at market prices - NNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost - Personal income
NNP at factor cost-Personal income-Personal disposable income
GNP at factor cost - NNP at factor cost - Personal income - Personal disposable income

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost - NNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **GNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost - NNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost is not correct.**
 
• **Gross National Product:-**
 
 
• It is the total market value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a given period of time, regardless of the nationality of the owners of the factors of production.
 
 
 
• 
 **Net National Product:-**

 
 
• 
 It is the GNP minus depreciation, which is the consumption of fixed capital.
 
 
 
 
• 
 **Factor cost:-**

 
 
• 
 It refers to the cost of the factors of production, such as labor, land, and capital.
 
 
 
 
• 
 **Market price:-**

 
 
• 
 It refers to the price at which goods and services are sold in the market.
 
 
 
 
• 
 **The expression GNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost is not correct, because GNP is already measured at market prices. Similarly, the expression NNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost is incorrect because NNP is already measured at factor cost.**
 
 
• 
 A correct expression for the difference between GNP at market prices and NNP at factor cost is: **GNP at market prices - NNP at factor cost = Net indirect taxes.**

questions.question: The book 'Rajatarangini' is about the history of which state written in 12th century CE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Rajatarangini**:-

 
 
• **It is a metrical legendary and historical chronicle of the north-western part of India, particularly the kings of Kashmir. **
 
• It was written in Sanskrit by Kashmiri historian Kalhana in the 12th century CE.
 
• It is about the history of the state of Jammu and Kashmir, written in the 12th century CE.
 
• The work consists of 7826 verses, which are divided between eight books called tarangas ("waves").
 
• The Rajatarangini provides the earliest source on Kashmir that can be labeled as a "historical" text on this region.
 
• Although inaccurate in its chronology, the book still provides an valuable source of information about early Kashmir and its neighbors in the north western parts of the Indian subcontinent, and has been widely referenced by later historians and ethnographers.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates from the Milam Glacier in Uttarakhand?

__
 
• **Gori Ganga:-**

 
 
• Gori Ganga is a river in the Munsiari tehsil of the Pithoragarh District, part of the state of Uttarakhand in northern India.
 
• **Its principal source is the Milam Glacier, just northeast of Nanda Devi along with the Glaciers of the Ralam River, and the Pyunshani and Uttari & Dakshini Balati Glaciers that lie on the western face of the Panchachuli Peaks.**
 
• The Gori Ganga flows through the Nanda Devi Sanctuary, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It is known for its scenic beauty and pristine waters. The river is also a popular destination for whitewater rafting and kayaking.
 
• The Gori Ganga joins the Kali River at Jauljibi, after flowing for a distance of about 104 kilometers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sutlej**:

 
 
• **The Sutlej is the easternmost of the five major rivers of the Punjab region. **
 
• It rises in the Himalayas in Tibet and flows through India and Pakistan before joining the Indus River.
 
• The Sutlej is a major source of irrigation water for both countries.
 
 
 
• **Ganges:**
 
 
• **The Ganges is the most sacred river in Hinduism and is considered to be a goddess. **
 
• It rises in the Himalayas in Uttarakhand and flows through several Indian states before draining into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Ganges is a major source of drinking water and irrigation water for millions of people.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna: **
 
 
• **The Yamuna is the largest tributary of the Ganges. **
 
• It rises in the Himalayas in Uttarakhand and flows through several Indian states before joining the Ganges at Allahabad.
 
• The Yamuna is a major source of drinking water and irrigation water for millions of people.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid bond in Alkenes that connects carbon atoms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double bond.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Alkenes:-**

 
 
• **These are hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond. **
 
• The general formula for alkenes is CₙH₂ₙ, where n is the number of carbon atoms in the molecule.
 
• **The carbon-carbon double bond in alkenes is formed by the overlap of one sigma bond and one pi bond. **
 
• The sigma bond is formed by the overlap of two hybridized sp2 orbitals from each carbon atom.
 
• **The pi bond is formed by the overlap of two unhybridized p orbitals from each carbon atom.**
 
• The pi bond is weaker than the sigma bond, and this makes alkenes more reactive than alkanes, which only contain single bonds between carbon atoms.

questions.question: In the context of mapping climate data, what term refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isoneph:-**

 
 
• **It refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud. **
 
• It is a type of isoline, which is a line that connects points of equal value.
 
• **Other common isolines include contour lines (elevation), isobars (atmospheric pressure), and isotherms (temperature).**
 
• Isonephs are used by meteorologists and climatologists to visualize the distribution of cloud cover over a region.
 
• **They can be used to identify areas of high and low cloud cover, as well as to track the movement of clouds over time.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isohels:-**

 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal sunshine duration.
 
 
 
• **Isocheims:-**
 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal temperature.
 
 
 
• **Isochalaz:-**
 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal hail size.
